verses.text: So all Israel were listed by genealogies; and behold,  they are written in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah was carried away captive to Babylon for their disobedience.
Now the first inhabitants who lived in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.
In Jerusalem lived of the children of Judah, of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim and Manasseh:
Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Perez the son of Judah.
Of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their brothers, six hundred ninety.
Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah,
and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;
and their brothers, according to their generations, nine hundred fifty-six. All these men were heads of fathers’ households by their fathers’ houses.
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of God’s house;
and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
and their brothers, heads of their fathers’ houses, one thousand seven hundred sixty; very able men for the work of the service of God’s house.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;
and Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph,
and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The porters: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers (Shallum was the chief),
who previously served in the king’s gate eastward. They were the porters for the camp of the children of Levi.

Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brothers, of his father’s house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers had been over Yahweh’s camp, keepers of the entry.
Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past, and Yahweh was with him.
Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the Tent of Meeting.
All these who were chosen to be porters in the thresholds were two hundred twelve. These were listed by genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer ordained in their office of trust.
So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of Yahweh’s house, even the house of the tent, by wards.
On the four sides were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south.
Their brothers, in their villages, were to come in every seven days from time to time to be with them:
for the four chief porters, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and were over the rooms and over the treasuries in God’s house.
They stayed around God’s house, because that duty was on them; and to their duty was its opening morning by morning.
Certain of them were in charge of the vessels of service; for these were brought in by count, and these were taken out by count.
Some of them also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
Some of the sons of the priests prepared the mixing of the spices.
Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that were baked in pans.
Some of their brothers, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the show bread, to prepare it every Sabbath.
These are the singers, heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, who lived in the rooms and were free from other service; for they were employed in their work day and night.
These were heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, throughout their generations, chief men. These lived at Jerusalem.
Jeiel the father of Gibeon, whose wife’s name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon with
his firstborn son Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. They also lived with their brothers in Jerusalem, near their brothers.
Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan was Merib Baal. Merib Baal became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz became the father of Jarah. Jarah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

footnotes.content: All Israel listed by genealogy, all the way back. Then the hard truth—Judah taken captive to Babylon for disobedience. Even in exile, the Lord does not abandon His people; He marks each name, remembering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After exile, the first to settle back in their own cities were Israel, priests, Levites, and temple servants. Not the powerful first—the faithful ones, ready to rebuild what was broken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem draws them back: Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh—tribes separated long ago now living side by side again. The Lord gathers His scattered children home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uthai returns, a name anchored in generations. He carries his lineage forward—a man known by his fathers, stepping back into the land his grandfathers held.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Asaiah and the Shilonites—Shiloh once held the ark of God, the place where Samuel heard the Lord's voice. Now these men return to serve in a rebuilt Jerusalem.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six hundred ninety souls from Zerah's line. The Lord counts each one; every name, every family matters to Him in this great return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Benjamin settling in Jerusalem. Once divided from their brothers, now dwelling in the same city, faithful to the God who calls them home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: More Benjamites named—Ibneiah, Elah, Meshullam, each a head of a household. The Lord rebuilds His people family by family, name by name, in patient love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nine hundred fifty-six men, all heads of fathers' households. Each one carries responsibility for his family and their place in the restored covenant community.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests return: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin—names that reach back to Aaron himself. The altar calls them home to serve again in the house of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azariah the son of Hilkiah, ruler of God's house. The high priest returns to oversee the sacred work—not a position of worldly power, but of service to the Most High.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: More priests listed—Adaiah, Maasai—each with their own genealogy, their own priestly line. The Lord restores His priesthood to minister before Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One thousand seven hundred sixty priests, very able men for God's service. Not chosen for their strength, but equipped by God for the work of His house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shemaiah the Levite, of the sons of Merari. The Levites return to their calling—to support and sustain the worship of God in His dwelling place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, Mattaniah—Levites whose names declare God's faithfulness. Each one finds their place in the restored work of praise and service.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Obadiah serves the Lord; Berechiah, whose name means 'the Lord blesses,' lives in the villages around Jerusalem. Even the suburbs become sacred space when the faithful dwell there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The porters at the gates: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman. They guard the threshold of God's house—a humble but holy trust, standing watch over the holy place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king's gate eastward—the ancient post where once watchmen served the kingdom. Now these porters serve Yahweh in the camp of the Levites, faithful to a higher kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallum the Korahite bears a name of an ancient lineage—his fathers kept the entry to Yahweh's camp in the wilderness. He continues their trust in a new generation, guarding the sacred threshold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past—a priest of old who turned back God's wrath with covenant zeal. His memory stands as a sign that the Lord rewards faithfulness with leadership.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah, porter of the door of the Tent of Meeting. Standing at the entrance—a place where heaven and earth touch, where holiness meets those who enter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two hundred twelve porters, chosen and listed by David and Samuel the seer, ordained in an office of trust. The Lord uses His servant leaders to establish faithful guardians of His house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The porters and their children watch the gates of God's house by wards—not a passing duty but a stewardship handed down through generations, standing watch over the place where the Lord dwells.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four sides guarded: east, west, north, south. The Lord's house watched from every direction, kept safe by faithful hands stationed all around it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every seven days the village brothers come in to take their turn at the gates. The whole community shares the watch—each tribe, each family bearing their part of this sacred trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four chief porters in office of trust, watching the treasuries and rooms of God's house. To be trusted with God's treasures—what a humbling calling, what an honor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They stayed around God's house day and night, their duty on them like a sacred mantle. The morning opens the gates—and the faithful are already there, ready to serve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Vessels brought in by count, taken out by count—the careful tending of holy things. Even in small details, the Lord calls us to faithfulness and order.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Furniture, vessels, flour, wine, oil, frankincense, spices—all appointed to faithful hands. Each item carries meaning: bread for hunger, oil for anointing, incense for prayer. The Lord's house lacks nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests prepare the mixing of spices—an art passed down, a craft by which holy worship is sweetened. Faithfulness shows itself in the smallest acts of care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mattithiah, firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, has oversight of the baked goods. Bread from the oven—the sustenance that fed the priests and the people, made with trust and order.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Kohathites prepare the show bread every Sabbath—twelve loaves set before the Lord. A sign of covenant, of God's presence, kept alive by faithful hands week after week.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The singers, heads of households living in the temple rooms, employed day and night. They lift their voices in praise—the sound of worship rising continually before the throne of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These are the chief men, heads of fathers' households, throughout their generations. In Jerusalem they dwell—pillars of the restored community, faithful leaders whose families anchor God's people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeiel the father of Gibeon, living in the city he founded with his wife Maacah. A household rooted and stable, ready to build and tend what God has restored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab—six sons named, each bearing his place in the family line. The Lord blesses faithful homes with many to carry on the work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, Mikloth—four more sons, the household full and fruitful. A large family speaks of God's blessing in the restored land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mikloth becomes a father himself, and all his line dwells in Jerusalem near their brothers. The generations continue—each one birthing the next, the covenant unbroken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ner, Kish, Saul—kings from this line. The genealogy traces toward David, toward the one who will sit on the throne of God forever. Even in genealogy, the way of the Lord becomes clear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jonathan the son of Saul had a son, Merib Baal. A bridge between the old king and the new; the line continues though the kingdom changed hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, Ahaz. Each name a child, each child a bearer of blessing into the future that God holds in His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahaz, Jarah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri—names strung like beads on a cord, one generation giving birth to the next. The chain of covenant runs unbroken through time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moza, Binea, Rephaiah, Eleasah, Azel—the line deepens and branches, each son a promise kept, each name a child known by God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azel had six sons whose names are remembered—Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, Hanan. Readers today hear an echo in this careful recording: the Lord knows each one. Every name matters to Him. Nothing is forgotten in His sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
